Severe Flooding Disrupts Economic Activity Across Kuwait

Kuwait is grappling with widespread flooding after days of torrential rain, with major highways submerged and businesses forced to suspend operations. The flooding, described as the worst in decades by officials, has disrupted economic activity across the country and continues to pose significant challenges as authorities struggle to respond.

Kuwait Petroleum Corp, the state energy giant, reported that some of its refinery operations have been temporarily slowed due to water ingress and logistical disruptions. “We are working closely with emergency services to ensure safety and to resume full operations as soon as possible,” a spokesperson said. “Our teams are monitoring the situation around the clock.”

The Chamber of Commerce and Industry said that hundreds of businesses in the industrial zones of Shuwaikh and Sabhan are facing losses. “We have never seen such levels of rainfall in such a short period,” said Khaled Al-Mutairi, a board member. “Deliveries are delayed, warehouses are flooded, and many workers cannot reach their workplaces.”

Kuwait’s Civil Defense Force has declared a state of emergency, with dozens of rescue operations underway. At least 1,200 residents have been evacuated from low-lying neighborhoods in Farwaniya and Jahra, according to local authorities.

Meteorologists warned that further heavy rain is expected over the next 48 hours. The Ministry of Public Works urged citizens to avoid unnecessary travel and to report any blocked drainage systems. Economic analysts predict that the flooding could have a lasting impact if the disruption continues into next week.
